The hon. member for Cape Breton South made his usual good contribution on coal. I intend to answer him on only one item at this time. He referred to the possible effect on the subvention of the increase in freight rates. Well, the actual increase of 12 cents a ton on coal and coke has now been published by the board of transport commissioners. The amount of the subvention payable is based upon the difference between the laid-down cost of Canadian coal and imported coal. In the case of Nova Scotia coal moving all-rail to the subvention area, that is the market area, the actual increase in freight payable will be 12 cents a ton less the 20 per cent assistance granted under the Maritimes Freight Rates Act, or 9-6 cents. On the competitive coal moving by rail from the United States mines the full increase of 12 cents will apply to the Canadian portion of the haul. The net effect, therefore, will be that while Nova Scotia coal will cost 9-6 cents more, the competitive coal will cost 12 cents more, which will mean a bettering of the competitive position in favour of Nova Scotia coal of 2-4 .cents.
Since this all-rail subvention is calculated on a percentage of the freight rate, that is 45 jper cent, and since the amount is small, the subvention rate will not be reduced to allow for this item. In the case of waterborne coal and railway coal, the subvention payable is directly determined from the laid-down cost of the competitive coals, and wnere there is any alteration in the competitive position from this or any other cause it is automatically covered by the subvention. I am sure that the Gordon commission will do a good job in its study of conditions in the Nova Scotia coal industry.

speechtext: Has the boundary never been surveyed between British Columbia and the Yukon and British Columbia and the Northwest Territories?

speakerposition: Minister of Mines and Technical Surveys
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND TECHNICAL SURVEYS
speechtext: It is being done at the present time, but it is not completed as yet.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND TECHNICAL SURVEYS
speechtext: Will this complete it?

speakerposition: Minister of Mines and Technical Surveys
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND TECHNICAL SURVEYS
speechtext: No, it will not be completed this year.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND TECHNICAL SURVEYS
speechtext: How much more is it going to cost to complete the work beyond this year? Is the minister in a position to tell us that?

speakerposition: Minister of Mines and Technical Surveys
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND TECHNICAL SURVEYS
speechtext: No, I would not like to hazard a guess, because it is extremely rough territory and we never know until it is completed. We have no estimate on that.

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND TECHNICAL SURVEYS
speechtext: Can the minister say what period of time will be required to complete the survey?

speakerposition: Minister of Mines and Technical Surveys
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND TECHNICAL SURVEYS
speechtext:
Are you speaking of
the British Columbia-Northwest Territories boundary?

maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND TECHNICAL SURVEYS
speechtext: Yes.

speakerposition: Minister of Mines and Technical Surveys
maintopic: DEPARTMENT OF MINES AND TECHNICAL SURVEYS
speechtext: I understand there has been a preliminary survey of the entire boundary but it was found there were inaccuracies, and some of it is being resurveyed at the present time. Today I saw the preliminary report on the Alberta-Northwest Territories boundary and we found there were some discrepancies or variations in two different locations involving, I think, seven or eight acres in each instance. Whether that will be resurveyed to be made exactly right or whether the provincial government will agree with the Northwest Territories representations that it is all right the way it is and that the original survey work be recognized as the boundary, we cannot say as yet. If we had to stay with it until it was absolutely perfect it might take quite a long time, but there are three parties concerned and we cannot say just how long it will take to complete.
